subject.title: [Feature]: Enrich before_tool_call event with action classification and input provenance

question: Should `before_tool_call` expose a stable action/provenance policy contract to plugins, and should that contract use an enum `actionCategory`, composable capability flags, minimized input provenance, or a combination?
rationale: This would define public Plugin SDK security-policy facts and decide how much provenance/session context third-party plugins may observe, which automation should not choose without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Approve narrow capability/provenance contract
options.body: Define a minimized provenance shape plus stable action/capability metadata, align it with the tool descriptor work, and require docs and compatibility tests before implementation.

options.title: Land provenance-only first
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/91800 as a partial security improvement and defer action classification to a separate SDK design item.

options.title: Keep current hook surface
options.body: Decline new hook facts for now and direct policy plugins to the existing `toolKind`, `toolInputKind`, `derivedPaths`, and trusted-policy surfaces.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow capability/provenance contract
recommendation.body: Define a minimized provenance shape plus stable action/capability metadata, align it with the tool descriptor work, and require docs and compatibility tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They have recent adjacent security/tool-block work and merged public hook-context changes, making them the best available owner for the security-boundary choice.
